title: Markov moves preserve the oriented closure
statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. If $\beta'$ is obtained from $\beta$ by a
conjugation or by a stabilization or destabilization in the sense of
[[def-markov-conjugation-and-stabilization-moves]], then
$\widehat{\beta'}$ and $\widehat\beta$ are equivalent oriented links.
strategy: Conjugation: the closure of $\gamma\beta\gamma^{-1}$ is obtained from that of $\beta$ by an ambient isotopy of the solid torus which rotates the base point through the loop $\gamma$ (equivalently, moves the cutting page), and this isotopy extends over the standard embedding in $S^3$. Stabilization: the closures of $\beta$ and $\beta\sigma_n^{\pm1}$ differ by a kink on the added strand near the axis; unwinding the kink is the first Reidemeister move performed in a small ball, and it realizes an isotopy between the two closures (both are built from explicit bands and the half twist $\sigma_n$). The inverse move is the reverse isotopy. The $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ assumption enters exactly through the smoothing lemma, which presents the closures of the given geometric braids as smooth oriented links; the isotopies themselves are the explicit local models, with the kink unwinding supplied by the R1 realization item.

references.title: Birman and Brendle, Braids: A Survey, Handbook of Knot Theory chapter, author manuscript; section 2 (printed pp. 12-26) and Figures 3-12
Traczyk, A new proof of Markov's braid theorem, Banach Center Publications 42 (1998), 409-419
